clue.text: Statement often repeated is mainly a source of manly danger

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so all but the final letter is kept

blocks.note: a trap set for people, a danger to men in particular

explanation.surface: Some repeated warning or saying turns out to be mostly about what threatens masculine men.
explanation.walkthrough: MANTRAP loses its last letter to leave MANTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or phrase chanted again and again, as in meditation, or a slogan repeated constantly.

clue.text: King Henry, taken in by false god, almost put up

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being placed inside it
almost means not quite the whole, so the last letter goes
in a down clue, putting something up makes it read from the bottom, i.e. backwards

blocks.note: Baal, the Canaanite god condemned in the Bible as a false idol
H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A monarch called Henry gets ensnared by an idol and is nearly hoisted up.
explanation.walkthrough: BAAL cut short is BAA; H goes inside to make BAHA, which reads upwards as AHAB. Fittingly, Ahab was the biblical king who worshipped Baal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahab was a king of Israel in the Old Testament, husband of Jezebel.

clue.text: Betrayal of new teacher over lines

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
RY is the abbreviation for railway, i.e. railway lines

explanation.surface: A freshly appointed schoolmaster is let down by something to do with lines handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the rearranged word sits over, i.e. above, the abbreviation for railway. Lines also suggests the punishment of writing lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachery is disloyal or deceitful conduct, the act of betraying someone's trust.

clue.text: An audit over a rising company gets the bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from the bottom upwards, so backwards
one word spread over another covers it on both sides, enclosing it

blocks.note: the article, as A
to vet is to examine or check thoroughly
CO is the usual abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm undergoing an inspection after its shares rise gets the boot, figuratively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets the bird' suggests being jeered at, but 'the bird' alone is the definition. In a down clue the reversed company rises inside the audit word.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with a long upturned bill.

clue.text: Categorise form provided by year

blocks.note: a form is a school class
provided that means on condition that, i.e. if
Y is the abbreviation for year; by puts it next

explanation.surface: Sort a document or form according to the year it belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is the British school word for a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: To classify is to arrange things into classes or groups, which is what categorising means.

clue.text: No light-hearted meeting-place where the effect of weight is felt

definitions.text: where the effect of weight is felt

blocks.note: first meaning, playful: a centre where seriousness gathers, the opposite of light-heartedness

blocks.clueFragment: where the effect of weight is felt
blocks.note: second meaning: the physics point at which an object's weight effectively acts

explanation.walkthrough: Gravity also means solemnity, so a centre of it is a meeting-place where nobody is light-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics the point through which the resultant weight of a body acts is its centre of gravity.

clue.text: Owned up to having been taken in

blocks.note: first meaning: confessed
second meaning: allowed to enter, received as a patient or member

explanation.surface: Someone confesses after realising they were fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' suggests deceived; here it means let in, as into hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Admitted means both confessed to something and accepted into a place such as a hospital or club.

clue.text: Plant in the borders, last put first

indicators.note: moving the final letter to the front rotates the word by one place

blocks.note: borders are edges

explanation.surface: A gardener moves the plant from the back of the border to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: The final S of EDGES jumps to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant of wet ground, a genuine plant name.

clue.text: Above normal level in musical instruction

blocks.note: first meaning: far louder than usual
second meaning: the Italian score marking telling players to play very loudly

explanation.walkthrough: Level here is sound level, not height, and the instruction is a marking on a score rather than a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortissimo, marked ff, directs performers to play very loud, well above ordinary volume.

clue.text: At sea rower can, though showing signs of distress

indicators.note: being at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An oarsman out on the water manages, despite looking worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Careworn describes a face or person marked by worry and strain, showing visible distress.

clue.text: Up-to-date way with the navy

blocks.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's navy

explanation.surface: The fleet's methods are bang up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means current or contemporary, belonging to the present time.

clue.text: Relieves tension by becoming less stuffy

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for settling a dispute or bad feeling
second meaning, literal: freshens a close atmosphere, as a storm does

explanation.surface: Someone eases an awkward situation by loosening up.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuffy suggests a pompous person; here it is a stale atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes ending friction by talking openly, and literally a thunderstorm refreshes heavy, humid weather.

clue.text: Unkempt beard on a Scotsman — this is one!

definitions.text: Unkempt beard on a Scotsman — this is one!

indicators.note: unkempt means untidy and disordered, so the letters are messed up

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Ian is the Scottish form of John, the stock crossword Scotsman

explanation.surface: A scruffy bearded Scot is offered as a typical example of a native of some place.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read straight it describes a shaggy-bearded Scot, who is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aberdonian is a native of Aberdeen, so a Scotsman by definition.

clue.text: Part of the orchestra on booze? Only the odd characters!

indicators.note: keeping only the odd characters means taking the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

blocks.note: the odd-numbered letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A musician who has been drinking? Only a few of the odd characters in the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd characters' sounds like eccentric players; it means the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a woodwind instrument and a member of every orchestra.

clue.text: Space not drilled in such a mine

definitions.note: an adjective phrase in effect: the answer describes the mine type

blocks.note: the open is open space, unenclosed ground
a cast hole or part is formed in a mould rather than bored out by a drill

explanation.surface: The ground left undrilled in a certain kind of mine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests mining with no boreholes, which fits the answer too: the mineral is dug from an open pit, not reached by shafts.
explanation.definitionFit: Opencast describes surface mining, where ore or coal is excavated from a wide open pit.

clue.text: Journalist is in post on time

blocks.note: a column is an upright post or pillar
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A reporter is at their post, punctual for once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is in post' reads as holding a job, but post is a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A columnist is a journalist who writes a regular feature, or column, in a newspaper.

clue.text: Make a comeback on the face of it

definitions.text: Make a comeback on the face of it

blocks.clueFragment: Make a comeback on the face of it
blocks.note: surface reading: a return to form that only looks like one, superficially
setter's reading: bounce back off a surface, as a bullet glances off a wall

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the face of it' is the idiom for apparently; read literally it is the face of a wall or rock that a projectile strikes and rebounds from.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebound off a surface at an angle is exactly what a deflected bullet or stone does.

clue.text: Bit of glass barrier, say, for fish

indicators.note: a bit of a word is just its opening piece, here the first letter
say signals that the barrier word is taken by how it is spoken

blocks.note: the first letter of glass
a railing is a fence-like barrier; spelt to match how it sounds

explanation.surface: A shard from a glass screen, perhaps, is used to catch fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Grayling sounds like G plus railing.
explanation.definitionFit: The grayling is a freshwater fish of the salmon family, with a large sail-like dorsal fin.

clue.text: Such an excuse is poor, fabricated stuff

blocks.note: first meaning: feeble and unconvincing, as in a weak excuse
second meaning: lamé, a fabric woven with metallic threads

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabricated stuff' looks like a made-up story to go with the excuse, but it means woven cloth, stuff being an old word for fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame excuse is a weak one, and lamé, written without its accent, is a glittering metallic cloth.

clue.text: Fix the value of a female animal?

blocks.note: first meaning: to evaluate, as for tax
second meaning, playful: a female donkey, the -ess ending as in lioness

explanation.surface: Someone sets a price on a cow or mare for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented word: ass plus the feminine ending -ess.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to estimate worth or value, while the joke reading makes a she-donkey.

clue.text: Wild moorlands, tho', demand illegal payment

indicators.note: wild means untamed and disordered, so the letters run riot

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Bandits on wild moors exact money from travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone to ransom is to keep a captive until a payment is extorted.

clue.text: Control vehicle in approach to house

blocks.note: first meaning: steer a car
second meaning: a private road leading up to a house

explanation.surface: Someone steers a car up the road to a home.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive is to operate a car, and a drive is a private driveway leading to a building.

clue.text: Split the split rate

indicators.note: a split word is broken apart and its letters can be put back in another order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Divide the divided charge again.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word does two jobs: the first Split is the definition, the second the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear is to rip apart, and a tear is a split in fabric.

clue.text: Extra call for this kind of delivery!

definitions.text: Extra call for this kind of delivery!

blocks.clueFragment: Extra call for this kind of delivery!
blocks.note: surface reading: an additional summons for a parcel or post
setter's reading: in cricket a wide is an extra run, called by the umpire when a ball is bowled out of the batter's reach

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a ball bowled is a delivery; one too far from the batter is called a wide, and the run it gives is an extra. A delivery that is somewhat wide might prompt that call.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball bowled rather wide of the stumps is fairly called widish, close to earning the umpire's signal.

clue.text: Lists came across backwards, one size being wrong

indicators.note: backwards means the word is read from its end to its start
a word that is wrong is out of order and needs its letters rearranged

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
to come across someone is to meet them
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A list-maker stumbled on lists backwards, with one size recorded incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: The I goes first even though one comes later in the clue. This is the American -ize spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemize is to set out item by item, so itemizes means lists in detail.

clue.text: A civil engineer's way on railway line

blocks.note: the indefinite article in its other form, an
CE is the abbreviation for civil engineer; the 's just links to the next piece
ST, short for street, is a way
RY is the abbreviation for railway; on places it next

explanation.surface: A civil engineer is laying a track along a railway route.
explanation.walkthrough: Line looks like part of the railway, but it is the definition: one's line of descent.
explanation.definitionFit: A family line is one's descent or lineage, which is what ancestry means.

clue.text: Fool not finishing act gets a rocket

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a sap is a gullible fool
a turn is a performer's act in a variety show

explanation.surface: A clown who never completes their routine is given a firework.
explanation.walkthrough: SAP loses its P to leave SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn V was the giant NASA rocket that launched the Apollo Moon missions.
